Constitutional amendment body: New idea on caretaker govt framework emerges
item.description:
The special committee on constitutional amendments has received a new idea regarding how an election-time caretaker government could be formed.

The idea emerged during an exchange of views between the committee and constitutional experts, law professors and Supreme Court lawyers on Saturday.

One proposal discussed at the meeting was whether a caretaker government could be formed from the upper house of parliament if the legislature had a bicameral structure. However, the framework for the caretaker government system has yet to be finalised.

Special committee chairman and Home Affairs Minister Salahuddin Ahmed told journalists about the discussions after the meeting. The meeting began at 11am in the Cabinet Room of the Parliament Building, took a one-hour break at noon and concluded at around 5:30pm. A total of 44 people took part.

Sources familiar with the discussions said proposals included establishing an independent secretariat for the judiciary; balancing the powers of the prime minister and the president; granting constitutional status to the Anti-Corruption Commission and the National Human Rights Commission; expanding the scope of fundamental rights; setting four-year terms for the lower house and six-year terms for the upper house; forming the upper house with representatives from all 64 districts and different ethnic communities; introducing direct elections to reserved seats for women; establishing an impartial selection committee for appointments to the Election Commission and other constitutional bodies; and transferring administrative responsibility for the control and discipline of subordinate court judges to the judiciary.

Some participants also questioned whether a bicameral legislature was necessary in a country like Bangladesh. Instead, they suggested establishing an advisory council. Other proposals included appointing opposition lawmakers as chairpersons of parliamentary committees on foreign affairs and home affairs, in addition to committees such as the Public Accounts Committee and the Public Undertakings Committee. Some also proposed enacting a law under Article 76 of the Constitution to strengthen the powers of parliamentary committees.

Sources said the meeting also discussed whether a higher court ruling could directly amend the Constitution. Most participants expressed the view that parliament would have to incorporate such a ruling into the Constitution through a formal amendment.

Caretaker government system

Speaking to journalists after the meeting, Salahuddin Ahmed said there had been detailed discussions on the process of forming a caretaker government and the scope of its responsibilities. A new idea had emerged on the issue, he said, outlining the proposal to the media.

Under the new idea, if an upper house of parliament is established, its term would not end at the same time as that of the lower house. The meeting discussed whether a caretaker government could be formed from the upper house.

In this arrangement, if the post of vice-president were created, the vice-president could serve as speaker of the upper house. An alternative proposal was to elect the upper house speaker with the consent of both the ruling party and the opposition. The speaker could then head the caretaker government, while the other advisers could also be appointed from the upper house with the agreement of the ruling and opposition parties.

Salahuddin Ahmed said these views had been put forward and could be considered. If further proposals emerged, the committee would include them in its report. Participants had been asked to submit their views in writing, he added.

He said the common view was that a caretaker government should be formed through consensus, excluding the judiciary and the president from the process. The discussion had been theoretical, he said, adding that written submissions on the formation process would help the committee. The committee would examine everyone's views, as it wanted the caretaker government system to be determined through consensus.

The issue of notes of dissent

Asked whether concessions would be made on issues where the Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) had submitted notes of dissent following discussions with stakeholders, Salahuddin Ahmed said no such decision had been taken.

He said the committee was inviting the opposition to participate in the process. If the opposition wanted the BNP to withdraw or relax its notes of dissent on certain issues, it would have to raise the matter before the committee. The committee could then consider the proposal.

Salahuddin Ahmed said the meeting had discussed constitutional and statutory bodies. The committee wanted to introduce a new definition called a “Statutory Constitutional Board”. The discussion covered whether a framework could be developed to determine how statutory bodies are constituted, define their responsibilities and ensure that they operate independently.

Experts also gave their views on the basic structure doctrine of the Constitution, the judiciary's power to review executive and legislative actions, and the judiciary's jurisdiction over constitutional amendments.

Regarding the establishment of a separate Supreme Court secretariat, Salahuddin Ahmed said the government had made a commitment on the issue. However, an ordinance issued by the previous government contained various flaws and had therefore not been enacted into law. The proposed separate secretariat remained under discussion by the committee, he added.

Achieving the objectives is what matters

Earlier in the afternoon, former interim government Law Adviser Professor Asif Nazrul spoke to journalists after leaving the meeting. He said he had also participated in a meeting of the parliamentary committee on constitutional amendments in 2011, during the Awami League government, when the committee was led by Suranjit Sengupta.

He had attended that meeting with high expectations but had subsequently felt betrayed. This time, he hoped to see positive changes. He appealed to everyone to keep the expectations raised by the mass uprising in mind.

Asif Nazrul said the caretaker government system should be determined on the basis of the opposition parties'' views. He and several other participants had called for the opposition to be involved in the discussion process. The committee had said it had made considerable efforts in this regard, he added.

Asked about the issue, Asif Nazrul said whether the body should be called a Constitutional Reform Council or a Constitutional Amendment Committee was a political dispute that he did not want to get involved in.
Personally, however, he believed that any change to the Constitution constituted reform if it was positive. What mattered most, he said, was whether the intended objectives could be achieved.

Among those attending the meeting were Professor Salimullah Khan, Professor Muhammad Ekramul Haque, Professor Borhan Uddin Khan, Supreme Court Bar Association President and Member of Parliament AM Mahbub Uddin Khokon, Bar Association Secretary Mohammad Ali, senior lawyers Shahdeen Malik, Ragib Rauf Chowdhury, Subrata Chowdhury and Manzil Morshed, among others.

Committee members attending the meeting included Chief Whip Nurul Islam Moni, Law Minister Md Asaduzzaman, Zainul Abedin, Planning State Minister Zonayed Abdur Rahim Saki, Mir Mohammad Helal Uddin, Social Welfare State Minister Farzana Sharmin and Shakila Farzana.

Bangladesh Jamaat-e-Islami Ameer Dr Md Shafiqur Rahman has questioned the home minister’s role in maintaining law and order, saying his primary responsibility should be to oversee his own ministry rather than serve all ministries.
“We are fortunate to have a home minister who serves all ministries. Yet his primary duty is to look after his own ministry. He has failed to control drugs or weapons, nor has he been able to restore order in society. There has been no visible improvement in the law and order situation in the country,” he said.
He made the remarks while exchanging views with journalists at the Moulvibazar Circuit House at 11am on Saturday during a 1-day organizational visit to his home district. It was his first visit to Moulvibazar since the national parliamentary election, drawing considerable enthusiasm among local party leaders and activists.
Speaking about the ongoing political situation, the Jamaat ameer questioned whether the opposition should remain silent amid successive incidents.
“Will we just sit back as one incident after another takes place? Will history forgive us? Why should the opposition take responsibility for the government's mistakes?” he said.
Shafiqur also criticized the appointment of political figures to district councils and alleged politicization of the Public Service Commission (PSC). He questioned why administrative officials had not been temporarily assigned responsibility for district councils instead of political figures.
Referring to past political practices, he said: “We have seen in the past that the government would even decide who would become the president and secretary of the opposition party. The media also helped create fascists, so the media must now work properly.”
Criticizing government statements on the law and order situation, the Jamaat ameer said: “Those in charge of the Home Ministry and important figures in the government often say that the law and order situation is ‘better than before’. But to this day, we have not understood what the benchmark for this ‘better than before’ is.”
Asked about Jamaat's participation in local government elections, he said the decision would depend on the political environment and circumstances.
“Nothing can be said with certainty without assessing the situation. The entire matter will depend on the political environment and circumstances,” he said.
Taking a swipe at the condition of roads between Dhaka and Sylhet, Rahman said: “There is no need to go to the Bay of Bengal to experience waves; you can experience the waves of the Bay of Bengal simply by travelling from Dhaka to Sylhet.”
He also outlined his party's position as the main opposition party, saying it would neither disrupt parliament to create instability nor blindly support every decision of the ruling party.
“As the main opposition party, we will adopt neither of these 2 positions: disrupting parliament to create instability or blindly supporting every decision of the ruling party,” he said.
Earlier, Rahman arrived at Sylhet Osmani International Airport at 8am, where senior leaders, including Jamaat's central assistant secretary general Ahsanul Mahboob Zubair, Sylhet metropolitan ameer Fakhrul Islam and Moulvibazar district ameer Engineer Shahed Ali, welcomed him.
He reached the Moulvibazar Circuit House at 9am, where a police contingent presented him with a guard of honor. He later delivered the chief guest's address at a conference for responsible ward leaders at the District Shilpakala Academy.
After Zuhr prayers, Rahman held a courtesy meeting with local leaders of the 11-party alliance at the Circuit House and attended a lunch.
At 2pm, a rukun conference was held at the Shilpakala Academy, attended by 600 rukons, to elect the Moulvibazar district ameer for the 2027–2028 session. Rahman addressed the conference as the chief guest, while Sylhet district ameer Maulana Habibur Rahman conducted the event.

item.title: Minister: Govt to take strict action to prevent abuse, misconduct in madrasas
item.description:
Religious Affairs Minister Kazi Shah Mofazzal Houssain Kaikobad on Saturday has warned that the government will take strict measures to prevent the recurrence of rape and other indecent incidents in madrasas, describing such incidents as “regrettable”.
He issued the warning while attending the triennial council session of the Bangladesh National Imam Samity at Agargaon in the capital in the morning.
Speaking to journalists after the event, the minister said imams had been instructed to raise awareness through Friday sermons and other awareness messages to ensure that such heinous crimes do not recur in sacred institutions like madrasas.
Addressing imams from across the country earlier, he urged everyone to remain highly vigilant so that no one could incite unrest and undermine religious harmony in the country.
Emphasizing the role of religious scholars in combating social crimes, Kaikobad said imams should speak strongly against drug abuse, terrorism and other social offences during Friday sermons.
He said imams enjoyed considerable public acceptance and influence in society, making their role important in raising awareness and preventing crime.

item.title: DSCC to file cases, seize goods from footpath shops
item.description:
Dhaka South City Corporation (DSCC) Administrator Md Abdus Salam has warned of immediate legal action and confiscation of goods from shops illegally occupying roads and footpaths, saying repeated warnings are over.
He made the announcements on Saturday during a special mosquito-control and cleanliness drive marking the DSCC’s weekly Cleaning Day program, held simultaneously across all 75 wards, said a press release.
Salam said illegal hawkers and makeshift shops contributed to traffic congestion, indiscriminate waste disposal and obstruction of pedestrian movement. “There will be no scope to occupy roads and footpaths in the name of humanitarian considerations,” he said, adding that shops operating outside designated rules would face legal action and confiscation of goods.
He further said the DSCC would launch another eviction drive in the New Market area next week, stressing that hawkers would not be allowed to set up shops on roads.
Emphasising cleanliness as essential to dengue prevention, Salam said stagnant water must not be allowed to remain for more than three days. Awareness campaigns and rallies would continue to help protect the environment, control air pollution and ease traffic congestion.
Regarding the removal of a secondary transfer station (STS) from in front of the Criminal Investigation Department (CID) office in Malibagh, he said it had been relocated at the CID authorities’ request, and the site had been converted into a parking area.
Construction of a new STS to manage waste from the surrounding area is underway and is expected to be completed by the end of this month, he added.

item.title: Police constable among 3 detained over drug use in Sreepur
item.description:
Three people, including a police constable, have been detained in Sreepur, Gazipur, on allegations of drug use, while police have recovered 120 yaba pills from a rented house.
The detainees were sent to jail through a court on Saturday afternoon, Sreepur Police Station Officer-in-Charge (OC) Mohammad Shahinur Alam confirmed.
The detainees are Constable Sarwar Morshed, 38, of the Traffic (North) Division of Gazipur Metropolitan Police (GMP); Sobuj Mia, 32, son of Mojibur Rahman of Keowa area in Sreepur municipality; and Jahangir Alam, 38, son of Abdul Kader of Bishnupur village in Rangpur’s Kaunia upazila. Jahangir was living in a rented house owned by Mosharaf in the Keowa Purbo Khanda area of Sreepur municipality.
Locals detained the three at a house near Keowa Bazar around 11:30pm on Friday and handed them over to police. Residents said Jahangir had rented the house about a month ago. They grew suspicious after noticing frequent visits by people suspected of using drugs.
On Friday night, locals caught the constable and another man allegedly consuming drugs and alerted police. Officers later raided Jahangir’s rented house and recovered 120 yaba pills hidden in different places inside.
OC Shahinur Alam said locals had initially detained two people, including the constable, while they were allegedly consuming drugs. Police later took custody of all three.
He said Sarwar’s identity as a police constable had been confirmed. A case was filed against all three under the Narcotics Control Act in connection with the recovery of the yaba pills.

item.title: Eminent journalist, former MP Shafiqur Rahman dies
item.description:
Muhammad Shafiqur Rahman, former lawmaker from Chandpur-4 (Faridganj), eminent journalist, freedom fighter, and former president of the Jatiya Press Club, passed away while undergoing treatment at a hospital in Dhaka on Saturday. He was 82.
Shafiqur breathed his last around 3pm at United Hospital in the capital. He was admitted to the intensive care unit (ICU) after suffering a heart attack at his Banani residence, family members said.
Born on September 25, 1949, in Krishnapur village of Faridganj upazila, Shafiqur earned his graduation and post-graduation in Bengali Language and Literature from Dhaka University in 1970 and 1971, respectively. He actively participated in the 1969 Mass Uprising and the 1971 Liberation War.
His journalism career began in 1970 with The Daily Ittefaq, where he served as staff reporter, senior reporter, and special correspondent over decades. He later served as two-time president of the Jatiya Press Club (2016-2018) and chairman and chief editor of Citizen TV.
Shafiqur was elected Member of Parliament from the Chandpur-4 constituency twice, in 2018 and 2024.
He leaves behind his wife, a son, a daughter, and numerous admirers.

item.title: Dhaka Central Jail inmate dies at DMCH
item.description:
An 18-year-old inmate of Dhaka Central Jail in Keraniganj died while undergoing treatment at Dhaka Medical College Hospital (DMCH) on Saturday.
The deceased was Mohammad Mehedi Hasan Kazi, son of Mohammad Faruk Kazi of Uttar Kazipara village under Shibchar Police Station in Madaripur.
Prison guard Md Sahabul Islam said Mehedi Hasan contracted dengue while in jail and initially received treatment at the prison hospital.
Later, he was transferred to the medicine department of DMCH on the instructions of the prison authorities.
As his condition deteriorated, he was brought to the hospital's emergency department around 3pm in an unconscious state, where attending doctor declared him dead at around 5:30pm.
Sahabul Islam said Mehedi Hasan was being held as an undertrial prisoner at the central jail (prisoner No-10718/26) in connection with a case filed with Kamrangirchar Police Station under the Women and Children Repression Prevention Act.
The deceased's elder brother, Sayed Kazi, said Mehedi Hasan was an SSC examinee. He had been in custody for the past seven months in connection with a rape case filed with Kamrangirchar Police Station.
He said his brother died after being taken to DMCH for treatment for dengue.
Inspector Md Habibur Rahman, in-charge of the police outpost at DMCH, said the body had been kept in the hospital morgue for an autopsy.
He said the body would be handed over to the family after the autopsy.

item.title: What happened at Tongi madrasah to draw bodybuilder father’s rage? Wife speaks up
item.description:
Authorities at the madrasah in Tongi, where a teacher has been arrested for allegedly inflicting a "bad touch" on one of his female students in Grade 1, have continued to insist that the teacher in question only promised to kiss his students as a reward for doing well in their exams, and never actually followed through on it.
This line has also been picked up by the society of alem-ulema at large, many of whom have spoken out against the student’s father for confronting the teacher and subjecting him to a public thrashing before he was arrested at the madrasah premises.
At the same time, many members of the same community have maintained that even if the teacher, Muslemuddin Ahmed, did kiss the girl, he was within his rights to do so as long as there was no ill intent behind the act.
According to the case statement, the alleged sexual harassment took place on the stairs of the madrasah’s ground floor last Monday.
Police have said their preliminary findings supported the allegations.
That has not stopped a wave of death threats from the community of Islamic scholars, and police cases against the father, Shahjalal Rumi, including one filed by the madrasah authorities for alleged vandalism at the madrasah premises, assaulting teachers, and looting Tk17 lakh from the principal’s office, as well as five mobile phones.
Almas Hossain, the madrasa’s founder and principal, has been claiming without any evidence to back him up that the incident had been orchestrated to damage the institution’s reputation. He also alleged that a group of 15 to 16 people, led by the child’s father, entered the madrasa and assaulted the teacher. He also said some of them were Hindus and suspected Rumi of being a "RAW agent".
Principal Almas said other teachers and security personnel were also beaten when they tried to intervene. He further alleged that the group vandalised the office and looted Tk17 lakh and 5 mobile phones.
Shahjalal Rumi, in a late-night press conference on Friday, admitted to breaking the glass top of a table he had struck in anger when he showed up there on Wednesday, but the offending teacher wasn’t being produced before him. He also promised to compensate the madrasah for that financially. He has denied the allegations of looting.
It is difficult to see how anyone could have looted the madrasah in those circumstances, in the presence of so many people. Even police arrived later to calm things down and take Muslemuddin away.
That he assaulted Muslemuddin is not in question. But he denied showing up with so many people and trying to create a "mob". He said he only took three of his friends with him. It may be noted that Almas Hossain in subsequent statements, seems to be dialling down that number as well.
From 15-16 on day one of the incident coming to light (Thursday), he has now come down to saying Rumi and his associates numbered 5-7.
But he has continued to insist that no kiss or "bad touch" - a somewhat euphemistic term for sexual harassment that parents may use to teach children how to recognise sexual abuse or harassment - actually occurred.
Muslemuddin apparently only promised to kiss all his students, that none of them complained to their parents, except Rumi’s daughter, and he in fact distributed chocolates among them.
In this situation, an important account has come forward of the victim’s mother, that is Shahjalal Rumi’s wife. It is important because it was to her that the daughter opened up after the incident last Monday, and she was the one handling the complaint to the school authorities.
She connected with fitness influencer A S Taj’s popular podcast show on Saturday, through her husband, who was there in the studio, to present her version of events, which is the closest we are going to get to the victim girl’s own version.
In her statement that lasted close to six minutes, the mother describes that on Monday, her daughter returned from her special Arabic class at the madrasah visibly upset, scared, and tearful. When prompted, the daughter revealed that her teacher, referred to as "Muslem Sir," had subjected her to "bad touch".
According to the mother's account, the teacher allegedly grabbed her daughter in the stairs after other students had left, knowing there were no CCTV cameras in that specific location, and kissed her in multiple places.
What made it all the more egregious was that the teacher also threatened the child with consequences if she told anyone. He also apparently tried to convince her that even if she did, no one would believe her since the stairs were not covered by CCTV and there would be no video evidence.
The mother initially contacted a female staff member (Luna Madam) who suggested giving the teacher another chance, which the mother found unacceptable. So she next spoke to the Vice Principal, Sakib Salehuddin, who was on holiday in his village home, but promised to install CCTV cameras on the stairs as well, and to ensure that a female teacher was always present during classes conducted by male instructors.
Both measures would be implemented immediately, the victim's mother was promised.
But the next day, on Tuesday, she learned that neither measure had been implemented.
Muslemuddin continued to take classes like before, and even allegedly told the daughter he "liked her," and obtained her home contact information.
That same day, the victim’s grandfather, Rumi’s father-in-law, informed the school principal, Almas Hossain, of what happened, according to the mother. Yet he has continued to deny knowing anything. Even on the day that Rumi turned up at the madrasah, he kept denying any knowledge of what had happened.
That day the mother also alleged that Muslemuddin even showed up at their home after school, repeatedly knocking and demanding the door be opened, which the mother did not wish to do since she was there alone with her children.
Rumi has separately said Muslemuddin turned up at his house on two occasions to ask for forgiveness. On one of these occasions, Muslemuddin ran into Rumi’s father-in-law and apologised profusely for what he had done, promising never to do it again. Rumi points to this as one of the incriminating pieces of evidence.
“Why would he ask for forgiveness if he did nothing wrong?” he asks. When he showed up at the madrasah on Wednesday, he was shocked to see the lack of initiative on the part of the authorities, and he was particularly triggered by the principal’s nonchalance, in particular his referring to the entire incident as a “silly matter”.
Later, once he manages to confront Muslemuddin, the videos circulating on social media show him visibly seething as the teacher presents his version. Once he gets to the part where he mentions “ekta chumu” (one kiss), the father of two cannot hold it in any longer, and his anger instantly explodes in the form of a rapier-like right hand that lands like a sidewinder on the teacher’s face and head, instantly felling him.
He then goes to town on him, kicking him on the ground, putting him in a headlock, punching at his guts and allegedly drawing blood from his skull, although the videos didn’t capture it.
Throughout this time, he can be heard saying “Kisher chumu re? Kisher chumu?” (“What do you mean kiss? What kiss?”).
That line has now become a rallying cry for many of his supporters on social media, where his actions have drawn huge support from many parents in particular, even as he continues dealing with threats of violence and arrest.

item.title: Police file GD over Rumeen Farhana’s spat with Sarail OC
item.description:
Police have filed a general diary (GD) over a heated exchange between independent MP Barrister Rumeen Farhana and Sarail Police Station Officer-in-Charge (OC) Monzur Kader Bhuiyan.
The GD was recorded following the incident on Thursday night, which became public on Friday evening. Police are also reviewing CCTV footage to identify people who accompanied the MP to the police station and allegedly engaged in disorderly or provocative behaviour.
Additional Superintendent of Police (Administration and Finance) Arafatul Islam said police record significant incidents through GDs as a formal measure. He said the entry was not a regular case or a personal complaint and that the situation remained under police control.
The incident has sparked conflicting accounts from the two sides. Supporters of Rumeen Farhana alleged that the OC had ignored repeated calls for security during her visits to Durga Puja mandaps.
The OC, however, said police were busy maintaining security across Sarail during the festival and could not assign a separate team to an individual. He also alleged that hundreds of people entered the station without prior notice and created tension.
Videos circulating on social media show a person accusing the OC of taking Tk 30,000 in bribes during the argument. The OC denied the allegation and claimed the person had been coached by the MP Rumeen Farhana, in response, referred to the OC’s political past.
The MP’s personal assistant, Zakir Hossain, said a two-page written list of alleged irregularities, corruption and negligence by the OC was being prepared for submission to senior police officials.
Rumeen Farhana said she wanted to be named as the number one accused if any case was filed over the incident. She said she submitted a complaint against the OC to the district Superintendent of Police on Friday, and was waiting for the authorities to decide on departmental action. She warned that she would announce further programmes if appropriate action was not taken.
The MP went to the police station around 8:00pm on Thursday to seek an explanation for the lack of security during her Durga Puja visits and to raise allegations of irregularities against the OC. She remained in his office until around 9:00pm.
According to Rumeen Farhana, she had called the OC eight to 10 times but he did not answer. The OC reportedly told her, “You are an MP elected by the people; the people will provide you security.”

item.title: Arsenal sink Everton to join City at Premier League summit
item.description:
Arsenal beat Everton 2-0 on Saturday to pull level with Manchester City at the top of the Premier League, rediscovering their taste for set-piece goals at a rainswept Emirates.
Ezri Konsa bundled the ball into the net in the opening minutes for his first goal for the club since joining from Aston Villa in August.
Fellow centre-back Gabriel Magalhaes doubled the home side's lead midway through the second period.
The win meant Arsenal took full advantage of City's 2-1 defeat at Villa Park in Saturday's kick-off -- the first time Enzo Maresca's men had dropped points this season.
Both teams are now on 21 points, but City, the Gunners' main title rivals in recent seasons, have a superior goal difference.
Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta was forced to shuffle his pack after Bukayo Saka suffered a muscle injury in the midweek Champions League draw at Bayern Munich, picking Noni Madueke and Eberechi Eze as his wide players.
Arteta was already short of wingers, with Christos Tzolis still sidelined and both Gabriel Martinelli and Leandro Trossard sold during the summer transfer window.
The home team started strongly and took the lead in the seventh minute after their third corner, following a scramble in the box.
Martin Odegaard's inswinging delivery was flicked on by Gabriel. Everton goalkeeper Jordan Pickford got his fingertips to the bouncing ball but it fell to Konsa, who poked it home at the back post.
- Set-piece kings -
It was the first non-penalty set-piece goal in all competitions in the current campaign for Arsenal -- who earned a reputation last season as set-piece kings as they won their first Premier League title in a generation.
Everton responded positively. Tyrique George's shot was deflected behind by Ben White but Arsenal were largely in control.
Madueke, recently deemed surplus to requirements by the watching England boss Thomas Tuchel, impressed on the right wing, spinning and hitting the side netting on the half-hour mark.
Arsenal had a major scare as the clock ticked towards half-time when a careless header from Ben White back to his goalkeeper David Raya was intercepted by Thierno Barry, but the Everton forward was unable to make clean contact and Raya made the save.
Gunners midfielder Mikel Merino flashed a header over the bar in the closing moments of the half, which ended with 13 shots and 10 corners for the home side, but just the solitary goal.
Gabriel went down in pain 10 minutes after the restart, stretching to intercept the ball, but was able to resume after treatment on the pitch.
Arteta made a triple substitution in the 68th minute, bringing on Kai Havertz, Bruno Guimaraes and Riccardo Calafiori.
Moments later they were 2-0 ahead when Gabriel rose to head home White's cross after a neatly worked move down the right.
Teenager Max Dowman, who became the youngest-ever Premier League goalscorer in the same fixture last season, was introduced for the final 10 minutes.
Everton almost pulled a goal back when Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall flashed a header just wide of Raya's post but that was the last major scare on a satisfactory day for Arsenal.

item.title: City beaten by Villa to end perfect Premier League start
item.description:
Manchester City's perfect Premier League start came to a crashing halt in a 2-1 defeat at Aston Villa as Nicolas Jackson's double extended an upturn in form for Unai Emery's new-look side.
Enzo Maresca had become the first manager to win his first seven Premier League games in charge of a new club but failed to find a solution to City's struggles at Villa Park, where they have now lost for the past four seasons.
After Jackson blasted home the opener after just six minutes, Villa relied on a brilliant goalkeeping display from Zion Suzuki to keep City at bay.
Erling Haaland breifly levelled early in the second half only for Villa to respond on the hour mark when Jackson drilled home Ibrahim Mbaye's cross.
"A fantastic day to share with our supporters in Villa Park," said Emery. "We felt that this is our fortress and the energy the supporters gave us was really fantastic."
Four years on from Emery's arrival, which has transformed the club from a sleeping giant into the Champions League, the Spaniard is working more magic despite seeing the spine of his squad in recent seasons decimated.
"He's just a tactical genius," Villa full-back Maty Cash said of his manager. "He's always got a new plan for something. He's always coming up with new ideas."
Six of the side that started Villa's victory in last season's Europa League final left during the transfer window.
But the recruitment of Jackson, Suzuki, Mbaye and Johan Manzambi is already paying dividends after a slow start to the campaign.
Until now City have managed to shrug off the cloud hanging over the club's Premier League future to keep winning on the field.
The 10-time English champions are appealing a guilty verdict on over 100 charges of breaking financial rules between 2009 and 2018 that could lead to swingeing sanctions, including relegation.
There was little sign of that distraction affecting Maresca's men, but they were made to pay for two sloppy defensive errors.
"I think we deserved more from the game for the amount of chances that we created and for the chances we conceded," said Maresca.
"We lost because we probably are not being clinical enough in their box."
A heavy touch by Marc Guehi presented Jackson with possession for the opening goal as he cut inside Elliott Anderson and blasted high past Gianluigi Donnarumma.
City largely dominated the remainder of the first half, but could not find a way past Suzuki.
Iliman Ndiaye, Rayan Cherki and Abdukodir Khusanov were all denied before Ndiaye struck the post.
City's pressure finally told on 52 minutes when Haaland powered in a header from Ndiaye's cross for his 13th goal in 10 appearances this season.
Josko Gvardiol nearly completed the comeback when Suzuki turned his blistering drive into the crossbar moments later.
Instead, it was Villa to got the decisive third goal.
Mbaye was played in behind the City defence and from his cross, Jackson's low effort should have been saved by Donnarumma.
The visitors pressed in vain for another equaliser to allow Arsenal the chance to move level on points at the top of the table when they host Everton later on Saturday.
A sixth win in seven games in all competitions for Villa lifts them up to sixth.

item.title: Late India charge seals thrilling second T20 win over New Zealand
item.description:
Tilak Varma struck a brutal half-century as India powered to a thrilling four-wicket win over New Zealand in the second T20 on Saturday for a 2-0 series lead.
The tourists scored 68 runs from the last 4.5 overs in Christchurch to clinch victory with a ball to spare, having looked down and out when they were reduced to 70-5 in the 11th over, in pursuit of 181.
Tilak carved 51 not out off 26 balls while Nitish Kumar Reddy struck the winning runs in an unbeaten 26 off 13 to hand India control of the five-match series.
The result matched their four-wicket win in the opening match at the same Hagley Oval venue two days earlier, which was achieved with two balls to spare.
Tilak said he never felt overwhelmed even as the required run rate grew.
"It was going through my mind, that I wanted to take the game as deep as possible and I have done it, so I'm really proud of myself.
"Nitish Reddy and myself, we're really happy that we've finished the game," said Tilak, who devised a plan to see off New Zealand's accurate spinners before unleashing against their seam attack at the death.
"There was definitely that intent. We wanted to push it into the gaps and run hard (against the spinners). They were really crucial, those runs.
"So we played smartly there and later on we know we can get success off the fast bowlers. We have finished off in style."
New Zealand's bowling was led by captain Mitchell Santner, who took 4-21 through the middle stages as India's top order failed to match their dynamic batting from game one, when they chased down 225.
Spinner Santner claimed the scalp of dangerous opener Abhishek Sharma for 27 in his first over and Naman Dhir for 31 in his fourth to have the tourists teetering at 112-6.
However, Tilak in particular swung the bat brilliantly over the closing stages, finding the boundary four times in the penultimate over bowled by Nathan Smith.
Santner lamented New Zealand's inability to close the door on the T20 world champions' deep batting lineup.
"You play a very good team, it's always going to be like that," Santner said.
"I think if we got one more wicket there, it was really game over.
"The way they controlled that chase, they made us make some errors at the end.
"Tilak and Naman Dhir and obviously Reddy at the end really played pretty well."
Vaibhav Sooryavanshi was dismissed for four, the 15-year-old batting sensation having been called into the side to replace the injured Ishan Kishan.
New Zealand's Glenn Phillips scored his second straight half-century as the hosts recovered from 41-3 to post 180-5.
Phillips struck four sixes in his 70 off 43 balls as he put on 116 in a fourth-wicket rearguard with Bevon Jacobs, whose 58 came off 46 balls.
Seamer Arshdeep Singh was India's best bowler, taking 2-33 off four overs.
Game three is in Wellington on Tuesday.

item.title: Rizvi: Imperialist forces carrying out planned cultural aggression in Bangladesh
item.description:
Acting Secretary General of the Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) and Prime Minister’s Political Adviser Ruhul Kabir Rizvi on Saturday said that subtle and planned cultural aggression is being carried out in Bangladesh.
“The imperialist forces are attempting to change the fundamental form of the language through conspiracy,” he said at a seminar organized by Sammilita Sanskritik Oikya on “The Crisis of Bangladesh’s Culture: An Exploration of Its Nature,” at Bangladesh Shilpakala Academy here.
In this connection, he said, no matter how many conspiracies are hatched, the people of this country have an inherent capacity to spontaneously resist any forms of aggression.
Rizvi said some new words were being deliberately introduced into the country’s language and culture. Replacing words that had been practised and used for a long time with new forms was part of imperialist activities, he added.
“We are witnessing subtle attempts to replace well-established words such as killing, blood and corpse with other words,” he said, adding that the nation had a glorious history of struggle and a history of shedding blood for its language.
Explaining the historical context and nationalism, the BNP acting secretary general said the so-called “Bengal Renaissance” of the 19th century was not a full-fledged renaissance in the broader sense.
“It was largely confined to Hindu revivalism, while the education and social reform needs of the predominantly Muslim peasant society of that time were completely overlooked, he said.
He added that the geographical and political identity of this country, or “Bangladeshi nationalism,” had developed through the course of those historical events and the struggles of 1947 and 1971.
Mentioning that a section of intellectuals had pandered to fascism during every crisis in history, he said just as many prominent intellectuals had lined up behind Hitler in the past, a similar phenomenon had been witnessed in Bangladesh during the period of fascism.
“They had not spoken out against enforced disappearances, abductions or the denial of voting rights,” he pointed out.
In contrast, he said patriotic intellectuals had always stood beside ordinary people and spoken the truth. Bringing cultural personalities together to discuss indigenous culture, national identity and heritage was a positive initiative, he added.
About the program, Rizvi said such events would encourage the practice of national culture and further strengthen efforts to preserve the country's distinct identity.
National Professor Dr Mahbub Ullah addressed the seminar as the main discussant, while Bangla Academy Award-winning researcher Dr Mustafa Majid presented the keynote paper with Sammilita Sanskritik Oikya President and freedom fighter MA Malek in the chair.
BNP Joint Secretary General and Member of Parliament Abdus Salam Azad; BNP Cultural Affairs Secretary and Film Actor Ashraf Uddin Ahmed Uzzal; Volunteer Affairs Secretary Mir Sarafat Ali Sapu; Ekushey Padak-winning rhymester Abu Saleh; and former Vice-Chancellor of Patuakhali Science and Technology University Dr Abdul Latif Masum took part in the discussion as special guests.
Other discussants included Rezabuddaula Chowdhury, film actor Helal Khan, eminent journalist Gaziul Hasan Khan and music director Ithun Babu.
Academics, litterateurs, writers, researchers, film and cultural personalities, and journalists attended the seminar.

item.title: When complainants become the accused
item.description:
A father seeking justice over the alleged sexual abuse of his child has himself faced allegations of assault, vandalism and theft in Tongi, Gazipur, while a separate confrontation between an independent MP and a police officer in Sarail, Brahmanbaria, has raised questions over security lapses and alleged police irregularities.
The two incidents have sparked debate over how safe the process of seeking justice is for ordinary people when those reporting wrongdoing face counter-allegations, legal complications or institutional pressure. In the Brahmanbaria incident, police recorded a general diary (GD) following the exchange.
Social media discussions have focused largely on the complainants’ conduct and the counter-allegations rather than solely on the original complaints.
Analysts say neither complainants nor accused individuals should be presumed guilty or innocent before an investigation. However, they stress that inquiries into the original allegations must not be overshadowed by counter-allegations.
An allegation of sexual abuse was raised against a teacher at a residential madrasa in Auchpara, Tongi, Gazipur, involving a child aged 6 to 7. According to the First Information Report (FIR) filed by the child’s father, the child was abused on the staircase on the ground floor of the madrasa on October 19.
After learning of the incident, the child’s relatives went to the madrasa on October 21 and questioned the accused teacher. The teacher was beaten by the relatives during the confrontation and was later rescued by police. On Thursday, October 22, he was sent to court after being shown arrested in the case filed by the child’s father.
The madrasa authorities subsequently accused the father and others of attacking and vandalizing the institution, assaulting teachers and staff, and looting Tk17 lakh. A separate complaint over these allegations was filed with the police station.
Denying the allegations, the father told journalists late on Friday night, October 23: “I went to the madrasa to seek justice for my child, not to create a mob.”
He claimed the madrasa authorities had been informed about the alleged abuse earlier but had failed to take effective action. Instead, he said, he was now facing threats. He called for an impartial investigation into the allegations against him and for security for his family.
Tongi West police station Officer-in-Charge (OC) Arifur Rahman said both sides had accused each other of issuing threats. He added that necessary action would be taken after an investigation.
A heated exchange between Rumeen Farhana, independent member of parliament for Brahmanbaria-2, and Sarail police station OC Manzur Kader Bhuiyan has also drawn attention.
On Thursday night, October 22, Farhana went to the police station to question the authorities about inadequate security during Durga Puja and allegations of irregularities involving police. She also accused the OC of corruption, taking bribes and neglecting his duties. Manzur Kader Bhuiyan denied the allegations.
Rumeen said she had taken a 2-page list containing information about local crimes and irregularities to the police station but had not received satisfactory explanations. The OC, meanwhile, alleged that the MP had arrived with a large number of followers and created unrest.
Following the exchange, police recorded a GD at the police station. A list of the people who accompanied the MP is also being prepared.
However, Brahmanbaria Additional Superintendent of Police Mohammad Arafatul Islam told the media that the GD was not a complaint. He said it had been recorded to document a significant incident.
In both Tongi and Brahmanbaria, the complainants’ conduct has become a subject of controversy alongside the original allegations. In Tongi, the allegations of assault and looting against the father have emerged alongside the allegation of child abuse. In Brahmanbaria, attention has focused on the MP’s visit to the police station and the ensuing tension, alongside her allegations of police irregularities.
Amid the competing claims, a key question remains: how much priority is being given to investigating the original incidents?
Dr Md Tawohidul Haque, associate professor at the Institute of Social Welfare and Research at the University of Dhaka and a crime analyst, told Dhaka Tribune: “An alarming trend in our society is that, in many cases, when people seek redress for wrongdoing, greater importance is given to the complainant’s behavior, position or identity than to the original offence. This creates a risk that the investigation into the actual incident will be overshadowed.”
He said: “The allegations of abuse against the child and the allegations against the father must both be investigated. However, counter-allegations must not become a tool for weakening the judicial process concerning the original offence. Many people are afraid to file complaints because of institutional power and social influence. They fear facing counter-cases, threats or social humiliation while seeking justice.”
According to Tawohidul Haque, law enforcement agencies must investigate impartially rather than treat complainants as adversaries. Otherwise, public confidence in the justice system could decline, potentially leading people to take the law into their own hands.
Ejazul Islam, executive director of the human rights organization Human Rights Support Society (HRSS), told Dhaka Tribune: “Seeking justice is not a favor; it is the constitutional right of every citizen. It is deeply concerning if someone seeking redress faces the prospect of further intimidation, counter-allegations or harassment.”
He added that such circumstances, particularly in cases involving child abuse, could discourage other victims from coming forward.
Ejazul Islam said: “In the Tongi incident, both the allegation of child abuse and the counter-allegations against the father must be investigated impartially. Similarly, the allegations of police irregularities raised by the MP must also be examined. A GD may be part of the legal process, but it must not become a means of placing undue pressure on anyone.”
Analysts caution that facing counter-allegations while seeking redress does not automatically mean someone is being harassed. At the same time, they say, counter-allegations must not be used to exert pressure on complainants. They stress that impartial investigations and accountability are essential in both cases, so that the original allegations receive due attention and all parties are treated fairly.

item.title: 10 killed in road crashes in 4 districts
item.description:
At least 10 people were killed in road crashes in Munshiganj, Jessore , Brahmanbaria and Narsingdi on Saturday, according to reports of our correspondents from the districts.
In Munshiganj, three people were killed and 16 others injured as a passenger bus plunged into a roadside ditch on the Dhaka-Mawa Expressway in the Hasara area of Sreenagar upazila in the district.
The deceased were identified as Md Ruknuzzaman Ronju, 50, the bus supervisor; Chanchal Biswas, 24, the helper; and passenger Salahuddin Ahmed Sakib, 32. All of them hailed from Chuadanga district.
The accident occurred around 3:00 am when the Dhaka-bound bus of Darshana Paribahan, travelling from Chuadanga, lost control while overtaking a covered van, crashed through the roadside railing and plunged into the ditch.
Deputy Assistant Director of Munshiganj Fire Service and Civil Defence Muhammad Shafiqul Islam told BSS that a rescue team from Sreenagar Fire Station rushed to the spot after receiving information about the accident.
The rescuers recovered the bodies of the three victims and rescued 16 injured passengers. Of them, 11 were taken to Sreenagar Upazila Health Complex for treatment, while the remaining five were released after receiving primary treatment.
Officer-in-Charge of Hasara Highway Police Station Md Soher Rana confirmed the incident, adding that the bodies were kept at the police station.
In Jessore, three people were killed and two others seriously injured in a head-on collision between two motorcycles on the Jashore-Benapole highway in Sadar upazila.
The accident occurred around 11:40pm near Natunhat intersection in Baro Meghla area under Diara union of the upazila.
Two of the deceased were identified as Siam Hossain, son of Shamim Hossain of Mondolgati area, and Ariful Islam Joy, son of Shahidul Islam, residents of Bojepara in Shankarpur of Jashore municipality. The third victim could not be identified.
Injured Omar Faruk and Rakib Hasan Rifat were admitted to Jashore General Hospital.
All three victims died on the spot.
Officer-in-Charge of Jashore Kotwali Police Station, Kabir Hossain, confirmed the matter.
In Brahmanbaria , two passengers were killed and 15 others injured in a head-on collision between a passenger bus and a truck in Sarail upazila of Brahmanbaria.
The accident occurred around 8:30am in the Bertala area on the Dhaka-Sylhet highway.
The deceased were identified as Sourav, from Parbatipur upazila of Dinajpur, and Asif. Further details about Asif's identity were not immediately available.
Abdul Halim, officer-in-charge of Khatihata Highway Police Station, confirmed the accident.
In Narsingdi, two friends were killed in a head-on collision between a motorcycle and a truck in Asharampur area of Raipura upazila on the Narsingdi-Raipura regional road.
The deceased were identified as Nirab Mia, 19, son of Selim Mia of Purba Para village in Radhanagar union, and Jibon, 20, son of Jahidul Mia of Saherchar village in the same union. Nirab was a Class XI student at Narsingdi Science College.
According to family members and local sources, the two friends had attended a concert in Narsingdi with several others. While returning home on Jibon's motorcycle, they collided head-on with a truck in Asharampur area.
Nirab died on the spot, while Jibon died on the way to Dhaka for advanced treatment after being taken to Narsingdi Sadar Hospital.
Faridul Alam, investigation officer of Raipura police station, confirmed the accident.

item.title: Fresh clashes rock France as protesters march on
item.description:
FRANCE-PROTEST/

Clashes erupted across France on Saturday as protesters took to the streets, a week after marches that degenerated into violence and prompted a firm security backlash from President Emmanuel Macron, who is scrambling to restore order.

Police arrested nearly 1,000 people as officers faced "an extremely elevated level of violence" from black-clad "ultra-left" extremists, Interior Minister Laurent Nunez said.

Riot police squads fired tear gas at protesters in the capital as well as in Marseille, Lyon, Bordeaux, Lille, Toulouse, Montpellier and Nantes.

Two people were "seriously" injured, Nunez said: one man in Toulouse, who reportedly had fingers blown off, and another person in Clermont-Ferrand. He did not give details of either case.

Authorities had deployed 70,000 security personnel across the country for the new marches, called to protest the cost of living.

France protests: Bangladeshi-owned shops also vandalised, looted; business owners anxious

The violence came a week after rioting that saw public buildings vandalised, hundreds of shops looted and 2,700 people arrested, casting a pall over the country six months before an election to choose Macron's successor.

Nunez said Saturday's outcome was more "positive" than a week ago, with more police on the streets acting more rapidly, conducting more pre-demonstration checks and better protecting businesses.

But there was widespread anger at the government over a protest crackdown viewed as an assault on the right to protest.

Saturday's demonstrations drew between 410,000 and 800,000 people across the country, according to different estimates by authorities and the organising CGT union.

The main Paris march had between 110,000 and 250,000 attendees, according to those sources.

Macron's government has ordered police to prevent protesters reaching city centres, where shops are concentrated, and in Paris and some other cities, partial curfews were imposed in certain urban zones.

France to deploy 70,000 police ahead of new protests

The French president had ordered non-union demonstrations be banned as "illegitimate".

In Paris, where many shops had boarded up windows to prevent looting, and the Louvre and the Musee d'Orsay museums shut for the day, the main demonstration passed off largely peacefully.

The march had been pushed to the capital's southeast rim under a last-minute order by authorities.

Afterwards, though, clashes broke out as the crowd was dispersing, with Nunez blaming "500 rioters" at the back of the march.

AFP journalists saw police charge several times, blasting tear gas and using batons against some, mostly young, protesters.

"They were just taking people down, you know, beating protesters," one demonstrator bleeding from a baton blow to his face, who gave his first name as David, told AFP.

‘How can French people do this to France?’ asks Macron condemning the violence

Ultra-right vs ultra-left

Thousands of protesters in the western city of Nantes broke through lines of police firing tear gas and a water cannon to reach the city centre, an AFP journalist witnessed.

Emma, 23, who came out in the northwest city of Rennes, denounced the bans on demonstrations and the "repression" of protests by high school students demanding better learning conditions.

Marching in the rain at the head of the protest in the northern city of Lille, 47-year-old Delphine insisted: "Neither the president, nor the weather will stop me from demonstrating."

In Lyon, police used tear gas to disperse around 1,000 people gathered in the south of the city.

"If they ban protests, that means we're heading more and more towards a regime that is fascist, that is dictatorial," said one 20-year-old protester in Lyon, who gave only his first name, Silem.

In the southern cities of Cannes and Montpellier, far-right activists clashed with "ultra-left militants", in what authorities said was an unprecedented development.

There was looting on the sidelines of the marches in Marseille and Grenoble, police said.

The Yellow Vests, who staged disruptive protests against Macron eight years ago, called for more demonstrations on 31 October for "the freedom to protest".

Mass protests in France spiral into worst riots in years

Far-left presidential candidate Jean-Luc Melenchon, who marched in Paris, said the movement "is going to repeat itself every week".

Le Pen protest

Tensions were heightened by a rally in the city of Orleans by far-right leader Marine Le Pen's National Rally party to kick off her campaign for the presidential election.

Thousands of counter-protesters chanting anti-fascist slogans marched in the city.

The unrest across France highlighted the febrile political atmosphere ahead of the vote, in which Le Pen leads in surveys.

Inflation in France, particularly affecting the cost of fuel, has surged since the start of the Middle East war in February.

"I'm going to try and instill a bit of optimism," said the four-time presidential hopeful, who has cast herself as the law-and-order candidate, ahead of her first major campaign speech on Sunday.

Protests have also broken out in Italy, Belgium, Spain and Portugal over different issues, yet with some overlap on inflation and education problems.
